memo.recommendation_rationale: Further diligence spend should be paused pending resolution of a high-severity red flag where customer maintenance agreements permit termination on notice without cause [p.11][p.19], directly contradicting CIM claims of 3 [p.11][p.19]-year contracted recurring revenue stability. While Meridian Mechanical Services demonstrates historical growth with 2024 [p.3] revenue of 18.4 [p.3] million and adjusted EBITDA of 3.1 [p.3] million across 310 [p.11] active customers, customer termination rights threaten the foundation of the contracted revenue model. Additionally, key deal elements—including executive equity ownership, asking valuation, and service-line gross profit breakdowns—remain unverified and pending review.
memo.business_overview: Meridian Mechanical Services, founded in 2004 [p.3] and headquartered in Columbus, Ohio [p.3], employs 142 [p.6] people and serves 310 [p.11] commercial HVAC customers across institutional and light industrial end markets in the Midwest. The company generates revenue through preventive maintenance contracts, emergency repairs, equipment retrofits, and building automation, reporting 58.0% [p.3] recurring revenue and having completed 1 [p.4] prior acquisition. Detailed operational descriptions, specific end-market exposure, breakdown of service lines, customer concentration metrics, asking price, and leadership equity ownership are unverified and pending review, as these fields lacked source page citations in the deal documentation.
memo.financial_summary:
Revenue grew from 14.2 [p.3] million in 2022 [p.3] to 16.1 [p.3] million in 2023 [p.3] and 18.4 [p.3] million in 2024 [p.3], reflecting a revenue CAGR of 13.8% [p.3]. Gross profit increased from 5.1 [p.3] million in 2022 [p.3] to 6.0 [p.3] million in 2023 [p.3] and 7.0 [p.3] million in 2024 [p.3]. Reported EBITDA expanded from 1.9 [p.3] million in 2022 [p.3] to 2.4 [p.3] million in 2023 [p.3] and 2.8 [p.3] million in 2024 [p.3]. Management adjustments diverge from reported figures, yielding adjusted EBITDA of 2.1 [p.3] million in 2022 [p.3], 2.6 [p.3] million in 2023 [p.3], and 3.1 [p.3] million in 2024 [p.3], corresponding to an adjusted EBITDA margin expansion from 14.8% [p.3] in 2022 [p.3] to 16.1% [p.3] in 2023 [p.3] and 16.8% [p.3] in 2024 [p.3].

Earnings quality appears baseline with total add-backs representing 8.1% [p.3] of 2024 [p.3] adjusted EBITDA, though specific adjustments require verification—notably an unexplained $0.07 [p.9][p.14] million legal settlement add-back in 2024 [p.9][p.14] despite management stating no material litigation exists. Furthermore, financial projections contain significant model conflicts: management projects 40.8% [p.15] revenue growth ($7.5 [p.15] million expansion from $18.4 [p.3][p.15] million to $25.9 [p.15] million) over 3 [p.15] years, but the sum of its four growth initiatives (9% [p.15], 5% [p.15], 7% [p.15], and 6% [p.15]) totals only 27% [p.15] ($4.97 [p.15] million), leaving 13.8% [p.15] ($2.53 [p.15] million) of projected growth unexplained. Days sales outstanding and individual service-line gross margins were omitted or unverified and remain pending review.
memo.thesis_commentary: The company scores fully against the services rollup thesis criteria, failing no target criteria across revenue scale, EBITDA margin, organic CAGR, customer concentration limits, contracted revenue share, earnings quality, entry multiple, and key executive retention. However, this screening fit is qualified because critical underlying inputs—including customer concentration figures, asking valuation multiples, and management continuity agreements—are pending review and unverified in the transaction documentation. Furthermore, while the business satisfies the quantitative contracted revenue threshold, the high-severity finding that customer contracts are terminable on notice directly undermines the stability assumed by the thesis.

red_flags.title: Customer agreements terminable on notice contradicts 3-year contract duration claim
red_flags.detail: While maintenance contracts are positioned as multi-year agreements driving predictable recurring revenue, the risk disclosures confirm customers can terminate on notice without cause. This undermines the stability and value of the contracted revenue base.

citations.quote: Maintenance agreements are typically three years in duration with automatic renewal provisions and contain customary assignment and change-of-control consent provisions.
Customer agreements may generally be terminated on notice. The loss of one or more significant relationships could have a material effect on results.

red_flags.title: Customer maintenance contracts require change-of-control consent
red_flags.detail: Customary change-of-control and assignment consent terms mean customer approval is required to transfer key maintenance contracts during a acquisition, creating closing conditions and customer retention risks.

citations.quote: Maintenance agreements are typically three years in duration with automatic renewal provisions and contain customary assignment and change-of-control consent provisions.

red_flags.title: Tuck-in acquisition growth initiative described using organic account target language
red_flags.detail: Initiative 1 is titled as targeted tuck-in acquisitions, but the descriptive narrative discusses identifying "target accounts" and onboarding field delivery staff, which describes organic sales rather than M&A.

citations.quote: 1. Densify the existing Ohio footprint through targeted tuck-in acquisitions

Management has identified an initial set of target accounts and estimates this initiative could contribute incremental revenue equivalent to 9% of the fiscal 2024 base over a three-year horizon, at contribution margins consistent with or above the Company's current blended margin profile.

red_flags.title: Cumulative 27% growth initiatives conflict with 40.8% projected revenue growth
red_flags.detail: Summing the revenue contributions across all four 3-year growth initiatives (9% + 5% + 7% + 6%) yields 27% of the FY2024 base ($4.97M), but the financial projections reflect total revenue expansion of 40.8% ($7.5M from $18.4M to $25.9M) without explaining the source of the remaining 13.8% ($2.53M) growth.

red_flags.detail: Asserting that tuck-in acquisitions and multi-state expansion into Indianapolis and Pittsburgh require no material incremental capital investment is unrealistic and masks the funding necessary for purchase prices and new operating hubs.

red_flags.title: Unsubstantiated $2 billion market size and market share claims

red_flags.title: Omission of executive professional history and equity ownership breakdown
red_flags.detail: The CIM omits executive background, prior career experience, and education for the leadership team, while also failing to disclose the equity ownership structure among the selling shareholders.

red_flags.title: Verbatim boilerplate copy-pasting across service lines, end markets, and case studies
red_flags.detail: All four service lines, four end-market segments, three customer case studies, and four growth initiatives use identical copy-pasted text paragraphs, reflecting low disclosure quality and obscuring operational distinctions across business areas.

citations.quote: Representing approximately 42% of fiscal 2024 revenue, this service line is delivered by dedicated teams operating under standardized procedures and quality controls. Management believes the offering is well positioned relative to local competitors given the Company's technical depth, response-time commitments and established customer relationships.

Management believes the relationship is stable and expects continued expansion under new ownership.
